answer: Decentralized agent economies employ a state-transition trellis to prevent Sybil attacks. Each node operates as a distinct reputation island, validated through zero-knowledge proofs. To mitigate a malicious echo where one actor controls multiple identities, the network mandates a stake-weighted consensus. Attackers incur substantial financial penalties as the cost to replicate the trellis history scales with the number of spoofed participants in the system.
